title: Show a running workflow's progress on the Claude screen
notes:
Claude Code's terminal shows a running Workflow (e.g. /pr-loop) in its footer: the workflow's name, a progress bar, agents done of total (1/2), elapsed time and tokens. Selecting it opens a panel: the workflow's description, its phases in a list (Conflicts, Round 1: Review, Round 1: Re-review, Round 1: Fix ...) with done/running marks and counts per phase, and the agents of the selected phase with model, tokens and time; keys to walk the phases, stop the workflow, pause, go back. Screenshots from the user, 2026-11-07.

The Claude screen shows none of it: while a workflow runs, main's screen only says it is waiting.

Change: the screen's foot shows a line per running workflow (name, bar, agents done/total, elapsed, tokens), like the background tasks line it already has. A key and a click open a panel with the phases and their agents, walked with the arrow keys (keyboard first, conventions-rule-1), with stop (and pause, if the SDK exposes it). Find what the Agent SDK streams for a workflow's progress (task or workflow events in the message stream) before designing; if it streams nothing usable, say so on the card instead of building a guess.

A key is a row in src/shared/keys/actions.ts and help.ts updates (keys-rule-2). Decisions in small modules with tests (workflow-rule-2). Docs: chat README, history.
